# Frozen revision 9 rack fades

The unchanged accepted `session_render.render_song` supplies every expected sample and gain. A trace observes its Double fade arrays, post-fade guitar/piano stems before focus or glue, and bass/drums/duck immediately before final mixing. The 63 accepted prefix events retain their original local timestamps, velocities, durations, and releases; `time` is explicitly set to `local_time` for the native local rack.

Two 13-second compressed-timing diagnostics place the outgoing tonal ramp at 1.6000078125–10.3000234375 seconds and the rhythm handoff at 5.900015625 seconds. The incoming case also fades tonal stems in over 3.25001171875 seconds, deliberately overlapping the outgoing ramp. Only the copied song duration, incoming-presence flag, injected prefix score, and `local_seconds` clock results change. The original renderer, fade formulas, summation, filtering, and bus gain order remain untouched. These are diagnostic schedules, not shortened versions of the accepted full-song mix. Original full-song timing is covered separately: two plans generated by the unchanged seeded planner retain their full allocation lengths, and original fade locals are captured with an empty score. No full-song audio is checked in.

The nine fields are raw faded guitar left/right, raw faded piano left/right, unducked bass left/right, processed drums left/right, and duck. Fade multiplication happens once on each summed Float32 stem with Double gains before drum filters. Drum filter tails persist after rhythm input reaches zero. Score-driven ducking continues for later kicks even when their faded audio is silent. Native scheduling uses its separately tested rounded shared transition endpoints; these oracle diagnostics preserve fractional reference endpoints by converting local seconds to Double frames.

Full-sample and per-component limits are maximum error `1e-5` and RMS error `1e-6`, fixed before native comparison. The 3,200-frame drum tail beginning at frame 188,801 has tighter `1e-8`/`1e-9` limits. Duck must match exactly. Guitar/piano are exactly zero from frame 329,601, bass from 188,801, and all audio is zero with unity duck from 400,000. Double gain probes allow `1e-12` for seconds/frame arithmetic reassociation. Native filter subnormal flushing may differ below the declared limits; tails are never removed from comparison.

Compact fingerprints include per-channel peak/RMS, boundary and regular probes, and complete Float32 hashes. Hashes identify the freezing platform and are reported alongside regenerated hashes; cross-platform acceptance uses numerical fingerprints plus full regenerated waveform comparison. Swift probes alone do not establish full waveform parity. Every fixture, candidate name, shape, finite value, original-source hash, and mandatory boundary is checked. No native output generates an expected value.

`freeze-fades.py` requires explicit `--replace` to replace reviewed fixtures and never runs in CI. `verify-fades.py --compare .build/tonal-native/fades --evidence .build/tonal-evidence/fades` produces eight 13-second Float32 WAVs: separate reference/native dry harmonic and rhythm pairs for both schedules, with hashes, LUFS, sample peaks, and four-times oversampled peaks. They are unmastered pre-glue/pre-room diagnostics, not final app audio. Earlier fixtures and all accepted v9 sources remain unchanged.
